hna.title: Eagle County Regional Housing Needs Analysis

local_funds.rate_text: 2% lodging excise tax (unincorporated county and Gypsum); additional 2% approved 2025
local_funds.summary: Eagle County Ballot Issue 1A (2022) created a 2% lodging excise tax on stays under 30 days in unincorporated Eagle County and Gypsum, with 90% for local-workforce childcare and affordable housing and 10% for tourism marketing. Voters added another 2% in 2025, for 4% total; the county describes the support that increase funds as childcare and public safety, so it is not counted as housing money.

Eagle County Good Deeds (since 2021, run by the Eagle County Housing and Development Authority) pays 15% of the purchase price, up to $187,500, for a perpetual price-capped deed restriction on open-market homes up to $1,250,000; ECHDA added $2.5 million in 2026 after its initial $4 million budget was nearly depleted.

local_funds.rate_text: 9% short-term rental tax
local_funds.summary: Steamboat Springs voters approved a 9% short-term rental tax in November 2022, effective January 1, 2023, restricted to increasing affordable and attainable housing; the Short-Term Rental Tax Fund is projected to end 2026 with a $52.6M reserve.

Steamboat Springs' Community Housing Fund, a special revenue fund set up by 2007 council resolution, was funded mainly by inclusionary zoning fees (repealed in 2019) and now receives loan repayments from the Yampa Valley Housing Authority.

local_funds.rate_text: 0.5% sales tax (groceries exempt)
local_funds.summary: Vail Ballot Issue 2A (November 2, 2021) raised the town sales tax 0.5% for housing initiatives, exempting groceries; in 2022 voters passed Ballot Issue 2I letting the town keep and spend excess collections from this housing sales tax.

Vail InDEED, begun in 2017, pays homeowners and buyers for a perpetual deed restriction requiring occupancy by people working in Eagle County; per Vail Daily the town provides 20% of market value with no income or appreciation caps.

Under Good Deeds Vail (2026), the Town of Vail and the Eagle County Housing and Development Authority each contribute up to 15% of a home's price (max $1.25 million) for a combined buy-down of up to 30%, capped at $375,000, in exchange for a price-capped deed restriction.
